subject: chemistry
question_text: Derive the relation between Kp and Kc for the following reactions: (i) 2HI(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + I₂(g), (ii) N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), (iii) 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), (iv) CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g).

AI chemistry check 2026-08-25. All four Δn values recomputed digit by digit and correct: 0, −2, −1, +1, with the matching Kp/Kc comparisons. Three memory tips rewritten for Rule 41 ('solids are silent / CO₂ speaks', 'one step milder', 'pulls'); the part (iv) common mistake was reworded because counting the solids also yields +1, so listing it as a wrong ANSWER was misleading. No marked line changed.

page_header: Chemical Equilibrium, Acids and Bases · 4 marks

steps.label: The working relation
lines: Δn = moles of gaseous products − moles of
steps.why: All four parts substitute their own Δn into this one relation, so it is written once at the top instead of four times.
common_mistakes: Recomputing the relation from PV = nRT in every part. State it once and substitute.
Defining Δn as reactants minus products. It is gaseous products minus gaseous reactants.
steps.memory_tip: One relation, four values of Δn. The whole question is counting gas moles.
steps.margin_note: No separate mark here — the four substitutions below carry the marks.

steps.label: (i) 2HI ⇌ H₂ + I₂
steps.why: Two gas moles on each side, so Δn = 0 and the factor (RT)⁰ equals 1 — the two constants are equal for this reaction.
common_mistakes: Counting HI once instead of twice. The coefficient 2 counts.
Writing Kp > Kc from habit. Here Δn = 0, so Kp = Kc exactly.
steps.memory_tip: 2 on the left, 1 + 1 on the right: Δn = 0 and the RT factor disappears.
steps.margin_note: Write Δn with its arithmetic shown, then substitute.

steps.label: (ii) N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃
steps.why: Four gas moles become two, so Δn is negative; a negative power of RT makes Kp smaller than Kc.
common_mistakes: Writing Δn = +2 by subtracting products from reactants. The order is products minus reactants: 2 − 4 = −2.
Leaving out the comparison Kp < Kc, which the sign of Δn gives.
steps.memory_tip: Fewer gas moles on the product side makes Δn negative, and negative Δn means Kp is below Kc.
steps.margin_note: The SIGN of Δn is the mark. Show 2 − 4 = −2.

steps.label: (iii) 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃
steps.why: Three gas moles become two, so Δn = −1 — the same direction as the ammonia case but one unit smaller in size.
common_mistakes: Counting O₂ as two moles. Its coefficient is 1; the count is 2 + 1 = 3 on the left.
Writing (RT)¹ by dropping the minus sign.
steps.memory_tip: 3 gas moles in, 2 out: Δn = −1. Same pattern as ammonia, with Δn smaller in size by one.

steps.label: (iv) CaCO₃ ⇌ CaO + CO₂
lines: CaCO₃ and CaO are solids, so they are not
counted. Only CO₂ is a gas.

lines.text: Kp = Kc (RT)¹ = Kc (RT),  so Kp > Kc

steps.why: Δn counts gaseous moles only. The two solids drop out, leaving one gas mole on the right and none on the left, so Δn = +1 and Kp is larger than Kc.
common_mistakes: Counting the solids as well. That happens to give +1 here too, but the method is wrong and it fails on other heterogeneous reactions — the correct count uses CO₂ alone. Writing Δn = 0 is the other error.
Forgetting the comparison: positive Δn means Kp > Kc.
steps.memory_tip: Solids are not counted in Δn. Only CO₂ is a gas here, so Δn = +1.
steps.margin_note: Part (iv) is the trap of the question — say in words why the solids are not counted.

insider_note: The mark in each part is the sign of Δn. Count gaseous moles only — part (iv) is the trap, where the two solids are not counted and Δn comes out +1.
